objectives.en: List the priority environmental issues of India
Explain the causes of land degradation and air pollution

narration.en: India has fertile plains, great rivers, dense forests and rich minerals. Yet our soil is eroding and our city air is choking. How did this happen?
narration.kn: ಭಾರತದಲ್ಲಿ ಫಲವತ್ತಾದ ಬಯಲು, ದೊಡ್ಡ ನದಿಗಳು, ದಟ್ಟ ಕಾಡುಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಖನಿಜಗಳಿವೆ. ಆದರೂ ಮಣ್ಣು ಸವೆಯುತ್ತಿದೆ, ನಗರದ ಗಾಳಿ ಉಸಿರುಗಟ್ಟಿಸುತ್ತಿದೆ. ಏಕೆ?

body.en: India has abundant natural resources: rich soil, hundreds of rivers and tributaries, lush green forests, plenty of mineral deposits beneath the land surface, the vast stretch of the Indian Ocean, and mountain ranges. The black soil of the Deccan plateau suits cotton, and the Indo-Gangetic plains are among the most fertile areas of the world. India has about 20 per cent of the world's iron-ore reserves. But development has put great pressure on these resources. The threat to India's environment is twofold: poverty-induced degradation and pollution from affluence and rapid industrial growth. The priority issues are land degradation, biodiversity loss, air pollution (especially vehicular pollution in cities), management of fresh water and solid waste management.

points.en: Rich soils, rivers, forests and minerals
Priority issues: land, biodiversity, air, fresh water, solid waste

narration.en: India is rich in soil, water, forests and minerals, but both poverty and affluence are damaging them. The priority problems are land degradation, biodiversity loss, air pollution, fresh water and solid waste.
narration.kn: ಭಾರತ ಮಣ್ಣು, ನೀರು, ಕಾಡು ಮತ್ತು ಖನಿಜಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಮೃದ್ಧ. ಆದರೆ ಬಡತನ ಮತ್ತು ಶ್ರೀಮಂತಿಕೆ ಎರಡೂ ಇವುಗಳನ್ನು ಹಾಳುಮಾಡುತ್ತಿವೆ. ಭೂ ಅವನತಿ, ಜೀವವೈವಿಧ್ಯ ನಷ್ಟ, ವಾಯು ಮಾಲಿನ್ಯ ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಗಳು.

title.en: On the board: Pressure on India's land

narration.en: Let us picture the pressure on India's land with simple bars.

say.en: Compare India's share of the world's area, people and livestock.
India has only about 2.5 per cent of the world's land area.
But it supports about 17 per cent of the world's people and about 20 per cent of its livestock.
Forests are thin too: about 0.08 hectare per person, against 0.47 hectare needed for basic needs.
Heavy pressure means soil erosion, groundwater loss and polluted air in cities.

body.en: India supports about 17 per cent of the world's people and 20 per cent of its livestock on about 2.5 per cent of the world's area, so pressure on land is heavy. Per capita forest density is only about 0.08 hectare against the 0.47 hectare needed for basic needs, and about 5.3 billion tonnes of soil are eroded every year. Land degrades because of deforestation, unsustainable fuelwood and fodder extraction, shifting cultivation, encroachment on forests, forest fires and overgrazing, not adopting soil conservation measures, improper crop rotation, indiscriminate use of agro-chemicals, poor irrigation management, groundwater extraction beyond recharge, open-access resources and the poverty of farm-dependent people. In cities, vehicles are a major source of air pollution, and the Central Pollution Control Board has identified seventeen categories of significantly polluting industries.

points.en: 17% of people and 20% of livestock on 2.5% of area
Forest: 0.08 ha per person vs 0.47 ha needed
Air pollution: vehicles and polluting industries

narration.en: India carries a huge population on a small share of the world's land, and its forest per person is far below need. Overgrazing, chemicals, deforestation and over-pumping of groundwater degrade the land, while vehicles and industries pollute city air.
narration.kn: ಪ್ರಪಂಚದ ಸಣ್ಣ ಭೂಭಾಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾರತ ಭಾರೀ ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯನ್ನು ಹೊತ್ತಿದೆ; ತಲಾ ಅರಣ್ಯ ಅಗತ್ಯಕ್ಕಿಂತ ತುಂಬಾ ಕಡಿಮೆ. ಅತಿಮೇಯುವಿಕೆ, ರಾಸಾಯನಿಕಗಳು, ಅರಣ್ಯನಾಶ ಭೂಮಿಯನ್ನು ಹಾಳುಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ; ವಾಹನಗಳು ನಗರದ ಗಾಳಿಯನ್ನು ಕಲುಷಿತಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

caption.en: Per capita forest area available (F) against the 0.47 hectare needed for basic needs.

narration.en: Move the slider to see how far India's forest per person is from what is needed.

tryThis.en: At 0.08 hectare, what share of the need is met? (about 17%)
How much forest per person would meet the need fully?
Why does a growing population lower F even if no tree is cut?

problem.en: India has about 2.5% of the world's area, 17% of its people and 20% of its livestock. Its forest per person is about 0.08 hectare against a need of 0.47 hectare. How many times the world average is the pressure of people and of livestock on India's land, and what share of the forest need is met?

steps.en: People per unit of land, relative to the world: 17 ÷ 2.5 = 6.8 times.
Livestock per unit of land, relative to the world: 20 ÷ 2.5 = 8 times.

answer.en: About 6.8 times the world's human pressure, 8 times the livestock pressure, and only about 17% of the forest need met.
